class.name: SignificanceBudgetPlanner
class.brief_description: Selects the highest-priority nearby actors for a bounded visual or simulation budget.
class.description: A native, stateless significance selector inspired by Unreal Engine's Significance Manager. For equal priority (0 to 3, higher means more important), closer distance wins, followed by the original candidate index. Results are ordered indices, not a mutated candidate array. Up to 16,384 candidates, 16 viewers, and 128 selection slots are supported. Invalid input returns an empty result atomically. The caller decides whether a selected actor receives HUD, VFX, audio or other optional work. Gameplay authority, visibility and physics are unchanged by the planner.

method.name: select_shadow_casters
method.description: Returns up to [param budget] stable source indices of eligible decorative shadow casters ranked by role (0 bush, 1 tree, 2 structure, 3 disabled), horizontal distance to world bounds, and current activation hysteresis. The three role radii are in order bush, tree, structure. Nonpositive radii disable their role. Existing casters remain eligible until radius + hysteresis, while inactive casters require a distance within radius - hysteresis. Active candidates receive a small ranking retention bonus; exact ties preserve source order. Invalid/nonfinite input, reversed bounds, mismatched arrays, over-16,384 candidates, and budgets outside 0..128 reject the entire plan. The caller owns actual shadow enabling and must not use this for gameplay visibility.

method.name: select_top
method.description: Returns at most [param budget] candidate indices ranked by descending priority and ascending nonnegative finite distance. [param priorities] must have the same length as [param distances] and values 0 through 3. [param budget] must be 0 through 128. No input state is mutated.

method.name: select_effects_visible
method.description: Selects up to [param budget] cosmetic effect indices, ordering by priority (3 to 0), then visibility (1 before 0), distance, and original index. Input visibility values must be 0 or 1 and have the same length as the other arrays. Four category caps and an inclusive hard distance limit apply. Invalid inputs reject atomically; off-screen critical effects still compete within their priority tier. This does not perform occlusion queries or affect gameplay authority.

method.name: select_top_priority_stable
method.description: Strict priority (3 to 0) ranks before distance. Within equal priority, currently retained IDs receive a distance discount capped at zero; actors past max_distance cannot be kept. Tie-breakers: real distance, positive stable ID, and input index. Arrays must match, IDs must be unique and positive, retained IDs must be unique and at most 128, budgets 0 through 128, distances finite and nonnegative. Range 0 to 1,000,000, hysteresis 0 through range. Invalid input returns empty, without mutation. Useful for temporally stable presentation budgets while keeping critical bosses prioritized.

method.name: select_top_stable
method.description: Selects at most [param budget] indices by distance with optional retention hysteresis. Current candidates whose stable IDs appear in [param retained_ids] receive a discount in their ranking distance, but cannot survive outside [param max_distance]. Equal adjusted distances compare raw distance, then stable ID, then input index. All candidates must have finite nonnegative distances, matching unique positive IDs, at most 128 retained IDs, a budget of 0 to 128, a range of 0 to 1,000,000 and hysteresis between 0 and the range. Invalid input returns an empty result without modifying any state. Designed for temporally stable visual, audio and animation budgets, not authoritative gameplay.

method.name: select_world_priority_stable
method.description: Ranks by priority (3 to 0), then nearest distance to any viewer. Previously retained positive stable IDs receive a distance discount only within the same priority, but never outside the inclusive hard radius. Ties use actual distance, ID, then input index. Supports up to 16,384 positions, 16 viewers, 128 selected and 128 retained IDs. Requires finite positions/viewers, unique positive candidate/retained IDs, valid priorities, and bounded finite range/hysteresis. Invalid input returns an empty array without changing state. Pure data operation; it does not change rendering, physics, or authoritative simulation.

method.name: select_world
method.description: Ranks candidates by priority, then squared distance to their nearest viewer; excludes candidates beyond inclusive [param max_distance]. Requires 1 to 16 finite viewers, finite positions, matching priorities, and a finite range between 0 and 1,000,000. No scene tree, rendering or physics work is performed.
